notes: All figures from Grab's FY2024 Form 20-F (fiscal year ended 31 December 2024), read as the '2024 Annual Report' PDF linked from investors.grab.com's Quarterly Results page. The file is hosted on s205.q4cdn.com, Grab's investor-relations host (Q4 Inc.), not on sec.gov. USD throughout. OWNERSHIP (as stated, not recomputed): Anthony Tan 3.7% of total ordinary shares and 63.2% of voting power at 15 February 2025, on 3,954,639,393 Class A and 119,498,676 Class B shares. His 151,123,290 Class B shares include 71,873,096 he holds himself; 19,492,330 held by Hibiscus Worldwide Ltd.; 15,206,161 he may acquire within 60 days from options and RSUs; 21,917,952 held by co-founder Tan Hooi Ling plus 7,243,301 she may acquire; and 6,215,298 held by Mr. Maa and the Maa Trusts plus 9,175,152 he may acquire. All of these are deemed beneficially owned by Anthony Tan under the Shareholders' Deed (proxy voting). The 3.7% therefore includes other people's shares that he votes, not only his own economic stake. The 20-F gives no separate percentage for his own shares, and none is derived. The table also excludes 1,111,904 Class B shares covered by March 2025 Voting Proxy Deeds; with those, footnote 3 says he controlled about 63.4% of voting power. HOLDERS: SB Investment Advisers' 9.9% is based on a Form 13F filed 14 February 2025 (footnote 4); asOf is that filing date. Uber and Toyota are as of the table date. DIVIDENDS: none; the cash-flow statement has no dividend line and the 20-F says Grab has never declared or paid a cash dividend. BUYBACKS: $226 million for 67 million Class A shares repurchased and cancelled in 2024 under the $500 million programme authorised in February 2024. STOCK COMP: $279 million equity-settled share-based payments (the 20-F also gives 'share-based compensation expense of $279 million' for 2024). GEOGRAPHY: Note 20 of the financial statements by country. At two decimals in billions the segments sum to 2.81 against a stated total of 2.80 (US$2,797 million), a rounding difference only.

ecosystem.notes: The 20-F says GMV also includes "(i) sales made through offline stores reported under the deliveries segment; and (ii) revenues made from products and services provided to driver-partners, merchant-partners and other customers to support their businesses, such as GrabAds and GrabRentals". Grab reports GMV only for its on-demand businesses (deliveries 11,724 and mobility 6,640, in $ millions); it stopped reporting financial services GMV. Total revenue (2,797) includes the financial services (253) and others (4) segments, which sit outside on-demand GMV, so Revenue / GMV slightly overstates the on-demand take. Deliveries revenue also includes Jaya Grocer supermarket sales. Revenue is after incentives: the 20-F says partner and consumer incentives have "the effect of which is to reduce revenue". The 20-F reports no total paid out to drivers and merchants, so payouts is null.
ecosystem.ratioNote: Grab revenue includes financial services outside its on-demand GMV, so revenue ÷ GMV is not a like-for-like share.

footprint.notes: Grab operates in eight countries: the 20-F defines "Southeast Asia" as Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam, with local offices in each. A list of countries with no figures is not a footprint row, so Cambodia and Myanmar have no rows. The 20-F gives employees only by function (11,267 full-time at Dec 31, 2024) and partner earnings only in total ($12.8 billion earned by driver- and merchant-partners in 2024); the 2024 ESG report gives employee gender split by country (including China, India and Romania) but no headcounts. Revenue by country exists in the 20-F but is already in the records. The only non-revenue country figures are loan receivables (credit exposure) for six markets, recorded as countries rows. Leased offices total over 107,700 sq m. The 20-F PDF is hosted on Grab's investor-relations CDN (q4cdn), hostType company.
